rv.q: "The book is the evening’s weak spot. The dialogue is sometimes so bald it could use an emergency toupet...Bolstered by ingenious, fast-moving, projection-enlivened scenery, expert choreography and sure direction, the cast have a platinum-plated ball...Confronting us with energy and spirit of that irrepressible order, the show moves beyond...
Wholehearted performances and the zest of a sizeable band go some way towards compensating for the rickety storytelling.
It’s a fascinating rags-to-riches story but this version leaves all the key questions unanswered.
Motown, the musical shines far less brightly, lacking smarts as well as soul.
This may not be a musical that breaks any records or leaves you emotionally charged from the story you have just heard.
The show moves beyond being a welcome nostalgia fest and becomes an urgent rallying cry for us all to rediscover our Motown mojo.
So, in many ways, MOTOWN is like a highly glorified karaoke drag show – yes, you admire the endeavour, but all the time you remember the greatness of the originals who are being portrayed.
Motown The Musical comes across as a muddled vanity exercise by Mr Gordy, still going strong at 86, and here credited as lead producer and librettist.
Motown The Musical is two and a half hours of musical happiness, and I had an absolute blast.
Squeezing the well-known hits into one show proves hard especially when there is a story to tell and the first half suffers from medley-itis at times.

cn.t: Critics find the Motown catalog irresistible but Berry Gordy's self-penned book weak and egotistical. The show divides opinion: some praise its energy and choreography, while others dismiss the shallow storytelling buried under truncated hits.
